title_en: Unexpected Item in the Bagging Area
description_ru: Саркастический монолог о противостоянии человека и кассы самообслуживания, где подозреваемым всегда оказывается покупатель.
text:
There is a moment, familiar to millions, when a person standing at a self-checkout machine ceases to be a customer and becomes a suspect. It begins with a small, cheerful voice, emanating from a speaker that sounds as if it were designed by a committee of nannies. "Unexpected item in the bagging area," it says. Nothing has been placed in the bagging area but a lettuce. I have placed it there myself, deliberately, and watched it fall into the grip of metaphysical doubt.

I do not know who first decided that shoppers should do the work of the cashier, and receive in return the pleasure of being accused. Whoever it was, I imagine him now, in a lakeside villa, surrounded by the lettuces of his triumph. The principle is admirably simple. The store removes the human being, and replaces her with a machine that is deeply suspicious of everything. The shopper, who has been promoted without a raise, is expected to scan, weigh, bag and pay, while a hovering attendant, nominally there to help, stares at the ceiling, as though pretending that he has never met me.

The machine, I have discovered, has a rich emotional life. When I scan a loaf of bread, it shudders slightly and informs me that I must "please wait for assistance," as if the bread had been involved in some unfortunate incident. When I scan a bag of apples, it asks me to select from a menu of forty-seven varieties, none of which appears to be an apple. When, in a fit of rebellion, I place my own reusable bag on the scale, it falls into a long, silent panic, then emits a sound like a small sigh, and the light on top begins to flash a lurid, accusing orange.

In the interest of science, I have conducted experiments. I have discovered that the machine will accept a banana, provided that I weigh it as "bananas, loose." It will decline a banana, however, if I weigh it as "banana, singular," on the grounds that this is an inappropriate level of familiarity. It cannot tell the difference between an onion and a very small cabbage, and will go on asking until I confess to a crime. It once informed me that I had "removed an item from the bagging area" when I had removed nothing but my hand. I apologised.

That, I think, is the real horror. I apologised. To a machine. Within three weeks of its arrival, a device the size of a refrigerator had reduced me, a mature man with a mortgage and a modest reputation for dignity, to murmuring, "Sorry, sorry, I'll just move it back," while a queue assembled behind me in the manner of a firing squad.

Naturally, the attendant eventually came. He is a gentle young man called Kevin, who is evidently paid to hold a key card, and who, with a mere flick of the wrist, can dismiss the machine's complaints in two seconds. This is the part that I find unbearable. The machine is not, as I had imagined, an infallible judge. It is a very nervous clerk, which reports me to the manager at the slightest hint of shifting weight, and which Kevin forgives, the way a patient father forgives a toddler, without ever really looking.

I have decided to make my stand. From now on, I shall use the human cashier, however long the queue, and I shall engage her in fulsome conversation about the weather, her day and the state of the nation. She will, I suspect, find this almost as annoying as the machine does. But there will be one great and meaningful difference: when I leave, she will say "Have a nice day," and, for once, she will not have been programmed to mean it.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Широко откройте рот: звук между «а» и «э».
Нижняя губа слегка касается верхних зубов, голос включён.
Губы вытянуты, без касания зубов; не «в».
Короткий губной звук, как укороченное «у»; не растягивайте.

questions.question: What does the machine say about the lettuce?
Who is Kevin?
questions.answer: The attendant who helps at the checkout.

questions.question: What did the narrator do that was the real horror?
What will he do from now on?
